questions.stem: A cuboid has a total surface area (TSA) of 94 sq. cm and a volume of 60 cubic cm. If its length is l cm, breadth is b cm, and height is h cm, l, b, and h, assuming all are positive and consecutive integers. Given, l<b<h. Quantity I: Find lateral Surface Area (LSA) of Cuboid. Quantity II: Total Surface Area of a cube with side is ‘b’.
options: Quantity I = Quantity II or no relation 2 www.bankersadda.com                                         |                               Test Prime
questions.explanation: We know, TSA = 2(lb+bh+hl) And, TSA = 94 sq cm Volume = l×b×h And, volume = 60 cubic cm Given, l, b and h are positive and consecutive integers We will try different combinations of l, b, h such that their product is 60 and the TSA condition holds. Let, l=3,b=4,h=5 Volume: 3×4×5=60 And, TSA: 2(lb+bh+hl)=2(3×4+4×5+5×3) =2(12+20+15)=2(47)=94 sq cm Both conditions follows, so l = 3, b = 4 and h = 5 Quantity I:  LSA of a cuboid = 2h(l+b) = 2×5×(3+4) =2×5×7=70 sq cm Quantity II: TSA of Cube with side = b = 4 cm TSA of a cube = 6×side² =6×4² =6×16=96 cm² So, Quantity I < Quantity II 10 www.bankersadda.com                                         |                               Test Prime

questions.stem: The speed of trains A (Sa) and B (Sb), in km/hr with Sa > Sb, are the roots of the equation x2 - 130x + 4200 = 0. Let Ta and Tb be their usual times in hours to cover a certain distance D km. If their speeds are swapped for the same distance D. (i.e. A travels at Sb and B travels at Sa), train A then takes (Ta + 2) hours and train B takes (Tb -2) hours. Find the sum of the original times (in hours), Ta and Tb.
questions.explanation: x2 -130x + 4200 = 0 x = 60 & 70 Sa = 70 and Sb = 60 D = 70× Ta D = 60× Tb Their speeds are swapped for the same distance D = Sb (Ta + 2) D = Sa (Tb -2) 70× Ta = 60 (Ta + 2) Ta = 12 60× Tb = 70 (Tb + 2) Tb = 14 Required sum = 12 + 14 = 26
